sections.h2: Which sale method fits a Rock Island owner?
sections.html:
You can hire an agent to list the house, market it yourself, or accept an offer from a buyer paying cash who will take the property as it is. Repairs, timing and whether the building is a home or a rental usually decide it.

Rock Island is one of the Quad Cities, alongside Moline and East Moline in Illinois and Davenport and Bettendorf in Iowa, so buyers come from both sides of the river. A tidy house can do well on the open market. A house that needs work, has a tenant, or sits on a rental-heavy block often fits a direct sale better. The trade-offs:

  • A listing reaches the most shoppers, though repairs and open-house hours usually come with it.
  • A private sale skips the agent's commission and leaves marketing, paperwork and negotiation to you.
  • A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, so you can often pick the closing day.
  • For a rental, the city's license and inspection rules come first.

Get the price, the closing date and who pays which costs on paper before you shake hands on anything.

Rock Island has about 36,225 residents, down from 37,108 at the 2020 census. Prices run modest: the middle value of an owner-occupied house is $125,900, and about 64.8% of occupied units are owned by the people living in them. The rest are rented, at a middle gross rent of $842.

That mix shapes who buys. Many sellers are landlords or heirs, and many buyers are local investors. An investor works backward from what tenants pay, so price a rental with area rents in mind. With values this modest, a repair bill can swallow a large share of the sale price, which is why owners of tired houses often look at as-is offers.

sections.h2: Older houses and what buyers ask about
sections.html:
Much of the city dates from the 1800s and early 1900s, especially downtown, around the Broadway Historic District, on Watch Hill and in the blocks near Augustana College. Houses from that era can carry original wiring, plaster walls and stone foundations. A buyer will want to know what has been updated, so gather receipts, permits and any inspection reports before you show the place.

If your address sits near a school district line, call the district before you advertise it. Rock Island-Milan School District 41 covers most of the city, while some southwest addresses belong to Rockridge. Plenty of shoppers narrow their search by district before they look at streets, so a wrong guess in a listing costs you credibility.

City ordinance requires a rental license for every residential rental, and each unit must pass an inspection against a minimum code standard before it is offered to tenants. Landlords apply through the city's self-service portal, and the Inspection Division emails to schedule the inspection after the rental fee is paid.

The owner or a designated agent has to be present. A $50 cancellation fee applies if nobody shows up or the visit is not canceled 24 hours ahead. A Notice of Violation lists items that fail life safety requirements. The first re-inspection is free, and each additional compliance inspection costs $50. The city can fine owners and revoke the license if repairs are not made in a reasonable time.

A license does not excuse unfixed violations. If you plan to sell a rental, clear any open violations or disclose them to the buyer in writing. The Inspection Division is at 1528 Third Avenue, and its staff can tell you where your license stands before you list.

sections.h2: Selling a rented house, step by step
sections.html:
You do not need a rental license to sell. The license covers renting a unit, not transferring it. Open violations on the file can still slow a deal, since a buyer's lender, inspector or title company may ask about them. A sensible order of work looks like this:

  • Call the Inspection Division and ask whether any notices are open on the address.
  • Fix life safety items first, because those are what trigger a Notice of Violation.
  • Pull together leases, deposit records and a list of repairs made.
  • Tell tenants in writing that the house is for sale, and agree on how showings will work.
  • Decide whether the buyer takes the house with the tenant in place or with the unit empty.

A cash buyer will often take a rental as it stands, tenants and open repair items included. That can save you the cost of bringing every unit up to standard before the sale, though you should still ask for the offer in writing with the closing date and any repair terms spelled out.

sections.h2: How a Rock Island deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for Rock Island parcels are recorded with the Rock Island County Recorder. The fee schedule, set by county ordinance effective February 1, 2025, is below. Any document with a legal description also needs the 10-digit PIN.

Rock Island County Recorder fees
Document typeRecording fee
Conforming document$83
Certain exempt document types$64
Non-conforming document, or more than five references$104

Your title company normally handles the filing, but ask the Recorder's office to confirm the current fee before closing.

sections.h2: Transfers that are exempt from state transfer tax
sections.html:
The state transfer tax statute exempts a list of transfers, and some of them still require the declaration to be filed. Section 31-45 of the Property Tax Code lists these among the exempt items:

  • Deeds where the actual consideration is less than $100.
  • Tax deeds and deeds of partition.
  • Deeds that only correct or confirm an earlier deed.
  • Deeds to or from government bodies and charities.
  • Deeds given to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or as a substitute for it.

A normal sale to a buyer does not fall in these categories, so expect the tax to apply. Rock Island County also offers a no-cost Property Fraud Alert subscription that sends a notice whenever a filing mentions you. If you will leave the house empty for a while, enroll before you go.

sections.h2: What a cash sale lets you skip
sections.html:
A straight cash sale cuts out the slow parts of a listing: staging, open houses, haggling over inspection repairs, and the wait for a buyer's loan and appraisal. Title still has to be clean, the contract signed and the deed recorded at the county. A rental's license and inspection history will still interest the buyer.

Check the written offer for the price, the closing-cost split, the closing date and whether the house goes as is. Keep a copy of everything you sign.

faqs.q: Do I need a city rental license to sell a rented Rock Island house?
faqs.a: The license applies to renting a unit, so selling does not require one. Open inspection violations can still slow a sale, so ask the Inspection Division where your file stands.

faqs.q: How much do Rock Island houses cost?
faqs.a: The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $125,900. An individual house can land far above or below that, depending on size, condition and block.

faqs.q: Where is a Rock Island deed recorded?
faqs.a: With the Rock Island County Recorder. The fee schedule effective February 1, 2025 lists $83 for a conforming document and $104 for a non-conforming one. Confirm the current figure before closing.

faqs.q: What school district is my Rock Island house in?
faqs.a: Rock Island-Milan School District 41 covers most addresses. A few in the southwest belong to Rockridge, so verify yours with the district.

faqs.q: What happens if my rental has an open violation?
faqs.a: The city can fine owners and revoke the license if repairs are not made in a reasonable time. Fix the items or disclose them to the buyer, and ask the Inspection Division about the file.
